Hi Bethany — looping in with a quick operations note: we've seen this behavior when an invite is forwarded or when a delegate/assistant has modified the event. Two practical workarounds that are low friction: 

1) Resend the invite from the original organizer mailbox (markus.k@redwood.com). That ensures Google/Outlook clients generate the native Join button.

2) Create a temporary Zoom meeting and paste the full join URL + passcode into the event description. Most calendar clients will pick up the change within a minute or two; if not, manually re-open the event or refresh the calendar cache.

A few gotchas to call out: calendar propagation can lag for cross-domain guests (sometimes 10–30 minutes); acceptance status may not appear immediately if attendees have multiple synced calendars. If immediate access is mission-critical, option 2 (Zoom link) is fastest.

If you want, I can take care of republishing the .ics after Ben posts the Zoom link so there's a canonical calendar entry. Markus / Ben, if you publish from the organizer account please include the Zoom URL in the description and set the event visibility to public (so Acme's corporate filters don't hide the join UI).
